correctness.rationale: The complete mixed-support-to-monochromatic-rectangle bijection is proved directly by enumerating possible T3 completions of each old directed edge. Discrete convexity gives row and pair-group coefficientwise bounds with a feasible simultaneous optimizer; strict convexity at z=1 forces all minimizer conditions. The maximum follows by removal of every rectangular consistency restriction and uniqueness by single-column and two-column rectangles. Algebraically exact formulas and equality enumerations are checked for all 299592 orientations at b<=6, and direct ternary-state extensions corroborate b<=3. This is a finite test supporting, not replacing, an all-order proof.

originality.rationale: The principal compared 2014 forbidden-tournament paper is about global typical asymptotic structure; it neither counts locally realizable singleton types over fixed oriented bicliques nor characterizes extremal three-row column patterns. The 2015 free-amalgamation treatment does not supply this finite-base graded enumeration, and the 2015 colored biclique work concerns monochromatic path/cycle covering. The result additionally differs in objects and quantified conclusions from nearby indexed Walsh-orientation and rainbow-connection results. The all-coefficient minimal polynomial and its exact mod-six equality class are not a corollary of these statements. Equivalent unindexed matrix enumeration remains a historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: A historical extremal enumeration of binary matrix monochromatic subrectangles could be equivalent under a change of language, including in literature not indexed by the searches.

Comparison with one specialized adjacent homogeneous multi-sorted directed-triangle case identifies a different forbidden substructure and type polynomial, but unindexed stronger transfer results may exist.
No independent mathematical or historical-priority audit has been performed.

value.rationale: This is a complete all-b coefficientwise classification for a natural nontrivial infinite family of finite bases in an established homogeneous structure. It identifies an exact mod-six balanced pattern in the six nonconstant three-bit signatures and exhibits exponential separation of mixed-shore extension freedom across orientations of the same underlying K_{3,b}; these are not merely numerical checks, trivial substitution, or a sequence increment. The exact extremizers also give a reusable discrete-convex design principle.
